items.title: 🤖 TOP 10 AI NEWS
items.summary:
🤖 TOP 10 AI NEWS

1. 🚀 Anthropic Unveils Claude Fable 5.2 & Mythos 5.2

Anthropic reportedly launched its most powerful models yet, promising 30% faster output and improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision.

💰 Fable 5.2 pricing: $8 input / $40 output per million tokens.

Mythos 5.2 remains restricted to verified organisations in specialised programmes.

The launch comes as Anthropic prepares for a potentially historic IPO.

2. 🛡️ OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber: A Major Cybersecurity Leap

OpenAI’s new security-focused model reportedly identified:

• 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities

• 948 working privilege-escalation exploits

• 81 high-severity Firefox flaws

The system reportedly used approximately $1.2 million in API credits.

With a “Critical” cybersecurity capability rating, access is limited to approved defenders.

AI-assisted security research is entering a new era.

3. 💰 Anthropic’s IPO Reveals Explosive Growth — and Rising Losses

Anthropic’s updated IPO filing reportedly shows:

📈 Quarterly revenue: $17 billion

📊 Revenue growth: 47% quarter over quarter

📉 Operating loss: $567 million

Despite rapid growth, investors are questioning the timing of its IPO and a potential valuation as high as $1.5 trillion.

4. 🤖 Nvidia Reveals GR00T 2 Amid CEO Scrutiny

Nvidia reportedly showcased GR00T 2, a 2-billion-parameter robotics model that achieved first-attempt success on 71% of tested robotics tasks.

Meanwhile, its board reportedly opened an independent inquiry into allegations involving CEO Jensen Huang and foreign intelligence activity.

Nvidia says it has no evidence that company secrets were compromised.

The company remains central to both AI infrastructure and physical AI.

5. ⚡ OpenAI Plans Shared ChatGPT & Codex Usage Limits

Starting in December, OpenAI reportedly plans to introduce a shared token allowance across ChatGPT and Codex for Plus, Pro, and Business subscribers.

Instant chat would remain outside the shared allowance.

The proposed change reflects the growing convergence of AI chat, coding, and autonomous computer-use agents.

6. ⚖️ US Justice Department Creates a Super Intelligence Task Force

The US Department of Justice is establishing a specialised unit to coordinate AI-related prosecutions and address certain state AI laws.

AI misuse, national security, and regulatory enforcement are becoming increasingly important government priorities.

7. 📉 AI Stocks Lose $2.5 TRILLION as Data-Center Opposition Grows

AI-related stocks reportedly suffered a massive selloff, erasing approximately $2.5 trillion from the Nasdaq 100’s market value in one session.

Meanwhile, voters reportedly supported restrictions on data-center development in 40 of 41 local ballot measures.

The message is becoming clear: AI growth faces financial, environmental, and infrastructure challenges.

8. 🔥 Meta Launches Ultra-Cheap Muse Ember

Meta reportedly introduced Muse Ember, targeting high-volume AI workloads with aggressive pricing:

💰 Input: $0.10 per million tokens

💰 Output: $0.50 per million tokens

Meta also reportedly acquired Conductor, a platform designed to run multiple AI coding agents together.

The battle for affordable AI automation is intensifying.

9. 🎓 Google Changes AI Access for Schools

Google reportedly announced that Gemini and AI-powered Search features will be disabled by default for K–12 student accounts unless administrators enable them.

Meanwhile, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash expands Google’s AI video capabilities, and Gemini 4 Carbon is being introduced to selected cybersecurity users.

Google is balancing rapid AI innovation with growing concerns about safety and access.

10. 🌍 Mistral Challenges Closed AI With Large 4

Mistral reportedly released Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter open-weight model, under a modified MIT licence.

The release could give businesses more control over AI deployment, infrastructure, and costs.

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

As districts consider their options, students are already seeing artificial intelligence become a more common part of everyday learning.

Some students believe the focus should be on establishing guidelines for AI use rather than banning the technology entirely. [...] San Diego County school districts face a January deadline to decide whether to opt in to Google's artificial intelligence features or lose access to the company's search engine, forcing educators to weigh the benefits of AI against concerns about student access to the technology. [...] Google plans to disable a range of AI-powered features, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search in January to give school districts more control over the technology students can access. items.title: Jensen Huang is living proof that AI’s rockstar CEOs are also a hidden risk | CNN Business

Huang has also served as the AI industry’s ambassador on the international stage. He recently met with leaders in European capitals, pitching them on the idea of sovereign AI, where every country needs to build and control its own AI systems.

And Huang has presided over Nvidia’s effort to build out the AI ecosystem. In September, the company disclosed a staggering $99 billion worth of equity investments in this space, up from $2.2 billion two years ago. [...] President Donald Trump, left, and Open AI president Greg Brockman, right, listen as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks at the White House in Washington, DC, on September 29, 2026, after meeting with top executives of AI firms.

When worries about cheaper open models from China sparked selling in global markets, Huang teamed up with Wall Street power players to cobble together a $500 billion plan aimed at keeping the flow of money pumping into AI-powering chips. [...] While Nvidia’s most recent annual financial report to regulators does not directly spell out how much the company’s fate is linked to Huang, the filing does note the company is “highly dependent” on the services of its executive team. It also acknowledges that “failure to ensure effective succession planning” could “hinder our strategic planning, execution and long-term success.”

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI Tries to Ease Backlash Against AI Data Centers
items.summary:
Broader rules and outside scrutiny would carry more weight than an individual company's promises, Perez-Etchegoyen said.

"OpenAI's own blueprint concedes that voluntary measures don't provide durable confidence. What would reduce uncertainty is the blueprint's proposals becoming law and applying to everyone who builds AI capacity, plus independent verification," he said. "Until then, enterprises should read this as a signal, not a planning assumption." [...] The company said it will disclose site-level water and electricity use, publish construction plans and commission independent noise studies before operations begin and then perform them annually afterward. The company says it will stop requiring nondisclosure agreements from public officials as a condition of negotiations, while retaining narrow protections for security and commercially sensitive information. [...] OpenAI said that the policy proposals build on work the company began in January when it announced its Stargate Community commitments to pay its own way on energy and develop plans shaped by local priorities.

"We followed with specific commitments in Georgia and Ohio, covering energy costs, water use, local investment and accountability," OpenAI wrote. "Today’s announcement is the next step in that ongoing effort."

## Why Eisman Calls OpenAI a Single Point of Failure

His logic runs through capital spending. If OpenAI failed, "the hyperscalers I am sure would cut back on their capex." He added that "this entire AI investment boom has become increasingly dependent on the success of just a few companies."
